title: Built my first game just as an AI workflow experiment (Lovable, PixelLab, Suno, ElevenLabs)
author: Exilon229
selftext:
Hey everyone! I don't have a game dev background at all. This is actually the first game I've ever made, and it started purely as a personal experiment to see what I could build with current AI tools.

It's called Nigredo's Greed, a small dark-fantasy action roguelite with 7-minute runs and a dice-rolling mechanic. Instead of using Unity or Godot, I built the whole thing on a web stack with Lovable (React/TS), which also helped me put the trailer together, and used Gemini whenever I got stuck debugging enemy waves and state issues. For art and audio, I used PixelLab for the sprites, Suno for the music, and ElevenLabs for some sound effects.

I originally exported it as a Windows .exe to test desktop packaging, but I just put up a browser version on itch so anyone can try it without downloading anything.

Since this was basically a test run, I'd love any honest feedback on how the combat feels or if the dice mechanic makes sense. Link is in the first comment!
